questions.q: In a user-item matrix, what does an empty cell represent, and what is the recommender's job?
options: An error in the data that must be deleted
A user who has not interacted with that item; the recommender guesses which empty cells a user would value highly
An item that no user should ever see
A user who has left the platform
questions.explain: Empty cells are unobserved interactions. Recommendation means scoring those unobserved cells and showing the highest-scoring items.

questions.q: Why is implicit feedback (clicks, purchases) harder to interpret than explicit ratings?
options: It is always false
It can only be collected once per user
A missing click does not mean the user dislikes the item; they may never have seen it
It cannot be stored in a matrix
questions.explain: Implicit signals are abundant but ambiguous: a click suggests interest, but the absence of a click is not evidence of dislike.

questions.q: In the lesson's popularity recommender, why are already-clicked items set to negative infinity before taking the top five?
options: So the user is never shown an item they already have
So the scores become positive
To make the sort faster
To give brand-new users personalized lists
questions.explain: Recommending something the user already clicked is pointless. Setting its score to minus infinity pushes it to the bottom of the ranking.

options: A model trains slowly when the server is cold
Recommenders only work in winter
Ratings must be collected in a cold-storage database
New users or new items have no interaction history, so collaborative methods have little to learn from
questions.explain: Collaborative filtering relies on past interactions. A new user has no row and a new item has no column, so the model cannot personalize for them yet.

questions.q: Which pairing correctly describes the two personalized recommender families?
options: Collaborative filtering uses item descriptions; content-based uses other users' behavior
Collaborative filtering uses other users' behavior in the matrix; content-based uses item attributes
Both use only item popularity
Both require explicit star ratings
questions.explain: Collaborative filtering learns from the user-item matrix alone, while content-based methods compare item attributes such as text or categories.
